claims.statement: Tom Allen shot and fatally wounded Tim Confoy in his saloon at 619 Market street just after 2 o'clock on the morning of 26 February 1899.
claims.excerpt: In a fight in his saloon at 619 Market street just after 2 o'clock this morning Tom Allen, the ex-pugilist, shot and fatally wounded Tim Confoy

claims.statement: Allen fired five shots at Confoy, and Confoy fell after the fifth.
claims.excerpt: as he fired the fifth shot Confoy fell, without a word

claims.statement: Allen said he recognized Confoy as a man who had been in the saloon on a previous night during the past week.
claims.excerpt: recognized Confoy as a man who had been in the saloon on a previous night during the past week

claims.statement: Allen said he had not produced his revolver until he saw Confoy try to draw his weapon.
claims.excerpt: he had said that he had not produced his revolver until he had seen Confoy make an effort to draw his weapon

claims.statement: Allen surrendered his revolvers to Officer Clifford.
claims.excerpt: To Officer Clifford, who was one of the first policemen to arrive, Allen turned over his revolvers and surrendered

claims.statement: Allen was taken to the Chestnut Street station and placed in the holdover.
claims.excerpt: Allen was hurried to the Chestnut street station, where he was placed in the holdover

claims.statement: Allen was later moved to the Four Courts holdover by direct order of Chief Pickel.
claims.excerpt: Later Allen was removed to the Four Courts holdover by direct order of Chief Pickel

claims.statement: Allen had been drinking heavily and was still under the influence of liquor when he was moved to the Four Courts.
claims.excerpt: Here he showed that he had been drinking heavily, for he was still considerably under the influence of liquor

claims.statement: Allen's saloon had been for years one of the toughest resorts in the city.
claims.excerpt: Allen's resort has been for years one of the toughest resorts in the city

claims.statement: Allen, an old prizefighter, handled the crowds in his saloon by brute force.
claims.excerpt: Himself an old prizefighter, he was able to handle the crowds by brute force

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: Oh, no, you're too bloody slow

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: Then, you bet your life, I let the bloody fool have it, and have it right.

notes: Confoy's wounds, the bartender's account and Spencer's injury concern other people and were not extracted. The hints on the holdover and drinking were kept.
